sentences.text: Vitirallus watlingi was a prehistoric flightless bird known as the Fiji rail or Viti Levu rail, distinguished by a very elongated and slender bill.
The genus name refers to Viti Levu, the island where it originated in Fiji, while the species name 'watlingi' honors the ornithologist Dr. Dick Watling.
Fossil remains were discovered in September 1998 on the island of Viti Levu, and Trevor H. Worthy first described the species in 2004.
The animal belongs to the genus Vitirallus, where the only known species is Vitirallus watlingi, which serves as the type species for the genus.
The animal lived during the Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene, with its time range recorded from 0.129 million years ago to the present Holocene.
